name: Vedant Fashions Ltd
title: Vedant Fashions Ltd - 543463 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 retail sales +3.4% and domestic SSG +3.8% with 65.7% gross margin, but closures ran ahead of openings and openings are deferred to H2, so supply growth is slowing while management claims competitor closures are starting.

triggers.quote: the number of stores have started to come down in these 8 states at least

triggers.label: Closures ahead of openings in Q1
triggers.quote: we were aggressive on closures in Q1, while we are aggressive on openings towards H2

triggers.label: SSG split half volume, half price
triggers.quote: it was a mix between volume and price, primarily right now, broadly half and half

guidance.value: Net positive financial year despite pressure; gross openings 3-4% tail, majority in H2
guidance.quote: we will still be looking at a net positive financial year

guidance.value: High single-digit SSG implied as doable (analyst framing, management said fair understanding)

summary.headline: Vedant Fashions Q1 FY27: revenue from operations up 7.2% to ~INR3,014 mn, PAT up 14.7% to ~INR81 crore, domestic SSG 3.8%.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations rose 7.2% YoY to about INR301 crore while retail sales to customers grew 3.4% to INR4,195 million, with domestic same-store sales growth (ex-SIS) of 3.8%. Gross margin was 65.7% and EBITDA margin 44.6%, with EBITDA up 10.8% and PAT up 14.7% to about INR81 crore (PAT margin 26.7%). Management cut store closures in Q1 deliberately ahead of its off-season, and framed H2 as the period for gross openings and growth. Management said the competitive environment is easing as weaker players exit, though it is too early to quantify the benefit.

financial_highlights.change: vs 65% in Q4 FY26; YoY decline attributed to GST (not in Q1 FY26 base)

financial_highlights.metric: Cash conversion (TTM June 2026, OCF/PAT ex finance income)

segments.name: Manyavar / Mohey (core wedding wear)
segments.commentary: Management said the Manyavar 'made for each other' campaign drew over 1 billion views. Mohey is growing faster than company average, driven by non-bridal categories such as stitched suits, sarees and crop-top lehengas.

segments.name: Twamev (premium)
segments.commentary: Management said Twamev outperformed the company in Q1 growth. Brand ran an influencer-led 'Truly You' luxury collection push.

segments.name: Diwas (value)
segments.commentary: Management said MBO/SIS bookings for Q2 are mostly complete and e-commerce deals are in place with Myntra, Amazon, Blinkit and Zepto. Q1 numbers did not reflect Diwas yet.

segments.name: MBO + SIS + e-commerce
segments.commentary: Combined, these are about 5% of revenue per management. Targets are described as aggressive; a new leadership team has been built for the vertical, and SIS is now split from MBO for separate tracking.

segments.name: International (UAE, North America)
segments.commentary: Management said UAE was hit by war and North America by tariffs over the last couple of months. No Q1 figure was given.

guidance_outlook: Management's core goal for FY27 is strong SSG, with H2 gross openings to follow. Management said the year will still be net positive on store count.
Management expects high single-digit SSG for the balance of FY27 to be doable, and agreed this was a fair understanding of its view.
Gross openings are guided at 3-4% of the store base as the typical annual tail. Openings will be more aggressive as rental pressure eases, mainly from end-Q2 and early Q3.

Q2 is the off-season, so closures were concentrated in Q1 to avoid carrying rentals into Q2. Management said Sep-Oct may be slightly weaker YoY, while November-March is expected to be strong and slightly ahead of last year.
ASP growth ambition for the year is slightly higher than current run-rate, with realisation gains expected from mid-Q2. Q1 SSG was split roughly half volume and half price.
capex_capacity: Net store closures were elevated in Q1 FY27. Management said closures are being driven by market shifts, relocation to larger stores, and weak-performing initial openings. Competition is not cited as a reason.
Franchisee capex is about INR2,100-2,150 per sq ft in Tier 2/3 cities and about INR2,500 per sq ft in Tier 1 cities.
Franchisee revenue per sq ft needed for good ROI is about INR7,000 in Tier 3, INR8,500 in Tier 2 and INR10,000-10,500 in Tier 1. Management said franchisee ROI is currently healthy.
EBO averages about 3,000 sq ft; SIS stores are a few hundred sq ft.
Management said the company is 'under-spent' on gross openings and expects to be more aggressive once rental pressure eases.
demand_pricing: Q1 SSG of 3.8% split roughly evenly between volume and price.

Industry: management said Tier 2/3 competitors that entered 3-4 years ago are closing, and internal state-level tracking (about 8 top states) shows net store closures. Management said it is too early to call market shrinkage or to measure the benefit of competitor exits; it wants 2-3 more quarters of data.
Management said Q3 product lineup and marketing investment give it confidence for H2. Campaign strategy is shifting from top-of-mind branding to conversion-led, social-media-driven campaigns.

Management said repeat business is a growing share of sales and a separate task force is driving it. A database of about 90 lakh customers is in use. Management said it will announce related plans on the next call if they materialise this month.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ~INR11,000/sq ft revenue threshold for franchisee economics correct, and is franchisee margin under pressure after GST?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave tier-wise thresholds: ~INR7,000 (Tier 3), INR8,500 (Tier 2) and INR10,000-10,500 (Tier 1). Management said franchisee ROI has been good in recent quarters with no pressure, and no change is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Why accelerate store closures if competition is the issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said closures stem from market shifts, cannibalisation by larger nearby stores, and weak initial openings, not competition. Q1 was targeted because Q2 is the off-season, so rentals were avoided.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin trajectory after GST and whether it stabilises at 65-65.5%.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 gross margin of 65.7% is up from 65% in Q4 FY26. GST was implemented around end-September, so Q1 FY26 was outside the GST base; from Q3 onward, the base is GST-inclusive.

qa_highlights.question: Why do primary (3-7%) and secondary (3-3.5%) growth differ, and what is inventory days?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly primary and secondary growth can diverge due to auto-replenishment and asked that it be judged on a full-year basis. Inventory was 34 days on a TTM June 2026 basis.

qa_highlights.question: Is high-single-digit SSG for the balance of FY27 doable, and what is the revenue growth path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said high-single-digit SSG is a fair understanding and that FY27 will still be net positive on stores. Growth will come mainly from SSG, plus the delta from new vs closed stores, net openings and MBO/SIS/e-commerce.

qa_highlights.question: What is the salience of MBO, SIS and e-commerce, and what are the Mohey and Diwas plans?
qa_highlights.answer: MBO, SIS and e-commerce together are ~5% of revenue, with aggressive growth targets. Mohey is growing faster than the company average. Diwas has Q2 MBO/SIS bookings largely complete, and e-commerce listings are set up.

risks_watch: Store count is shrinking through closures, and FY27 SSG depends on H2 (Q3 and Q4) recovery. Management guided Sep-Oct to be weaker YoY, before the Nov-March wedding season.
International: UAE (war) and North America (tariffs) are both under pressure, with no timeline for recovery given.
Gross margin YoY comparisons are distorted by GST until Q3 FY27. The stated base case is 65-65.5% from Q2 onward.
Management wants 2-3 more quarters to judge whether competitor exits are lifting its own sales.
ASP growth ambition is 'slightly higher' than the current run-rate and only starts to bite from mid-Q2. Price vs volume mix will be a watch item.
Management said it will announce a repeat-business plan in the next call if it materialises this month.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins, cash conversion and H2 product and marketing plans, but cautious on near-term SSG and store growth. Management was evasive on specific store-level economics (new-store productivity uplift, international revenue) and did not quantify the benefit from competitor exits.
key_quotes: Hence, we were aggressive on closures in Q1, while we are aggressive on openings towards H2 because that's where majority of our business is.
I have never faced a reason for a closure to be competition.
So, I think definitely, that intensity will go down.
So, I think I'm really confident with the kind of product lineup we have ready for Q3.

adds.what: Gross store openings at 3-4% of store base as annual tail, weighted to H2 (end-Q2 / early Q3 onward)

growth.why: Management targets high single-digit SSG for the balance of FY27 (analyst framing it accepted as fair) and a net-positive store count, with 3-4% gross openings weighted to H2; backing is partial, citing ASP realisation from mid-Q2, a Q3 product lineup and competitor exits that management says are too early to quantify, with no specific capacity or order numbers.
